text:
Nina (runtime): Heads-up — canary started hitting intermittent OOMs on long-chat workload (8k seq). stack traces point at scratchpad/tensor-pool path, looks like a concurrency reuse issue. I dumped a CUPTI timeline and a short repro. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Alex: Hmm, sounds like the slot gets handed back and immediately reused while another request still has a stale pointer. We saw a similar failure mode when we did buffer lending for logits. Could be freelist compaction + racing frees. :thinking_face: 

Sam: Repro I used locally:
```
# repro
./bin/loadgen --model redwood-v1 --seq 8192 --concurrency 12 --mode chat --kv_cache=true
```
Run for ~30s and you'll see p99 OOMs on canary.

Lee: Quick snippet from the allocation timeline (CUPTI-ish output) — overlapping alloc/free on same slab id: 
```
[alloc] t=0.0010s size=6.4MB slab=3 owner=req-42
[free]  t=0.0012s slab=3 owner=req-41
[alloc] t=0.0013s size=6.4MB slab=3 owner=req-42  <-- reuse while req-41 still touching
```
This pattern matches a race where a free races with a delayed device memcpy/readback.

Maria: Two mitigation ideas: (1) simple: add an epoch tag to a slab/slot and only allow reuse if slot.epoch <= global_epoch, bump epoch on compaction; (2) pragmatic: add a cheap concurrency fence around compaction/eviction (coarse but low-risk) and increase freelist compaction threshold from 0.2 -> 0.35 to reduce churn.

Alex: Epoch tagging is nice — basically lease-based reuse. Also add per-request borrow token so frees check token == current. That avoids CAS hot paths but blocks rare races.

Nina (runtime): For rollout I want minimal blast radius. Plan: implement fallback path so if the allocator detects a double-claim or an OOM on pooled path, we fallback to cudaMalloc path and emit metric runtime.pool.fallback with context tags. Then roll as feature-flag disabled -> enable on 10% canary -> 50% -> full if stable.

Sam: I prototyped a quick epoch variant and ran microbench; results vs master (local, same hardware):
- resident mem: master 9.2GB -> epoch-proto 7.6GB (~18% reduction)
- p50 latency: master 24.1ms -> epoch-proto 23.6ms (~2% improvement)
So memory looks better and perf is roughly equal. No OOM during 5k req run.

Lee: Small implementation note: when you add epoch, ensure we store epoch in device-visible header or shadow table — avoid host-only checks because compaction may reorder device operations. Also add a small grace period (ms) before reuse to let inflight device ops settle.

Alex: Also consider tagging by buffer "kind" (activation vs logits vs scratchpad). Logits buffers tend to be reused across batch/position; activations are larger and shorter-lived. Different heuristics per kind helped earlier.

Nina (runtime): Cool. I'll open the PR with two commits: (A) pool fallback + metric + feature flag, (B) epoch-based reuse + unit tests. CI bot will run perf bench; if the canary still sees OOMs, flag will stay off.

ci-bot: build #3421 queued for runtime (tests + microbench).

Sam: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1234 (proto, do not merge). Includes repro script and the CUPTI sample.

Maria: If we need a fast hotfix, we can also temporarily disable freelist compaction on canary: set ENV POOL_COMPACT=0. That reduces reuse but should stop races immediately while we validate epoch approach.

Nina (runtime): SGTM. I'm going to schedule the canary run with POOL_COMPACT=0 for the next deploy window and keep the PR moving. Will update thread with results after 24h. :thumbsup: :eyes:
